question.text: In valuation, Enterprise Value to Equity Value bridge requires:

answer.text: Adding cash and subtracting debt from enterprise value
Subtracting debt, minority interest, and preferred capital from enterprise value, then adding cash and non-operating investments
Simply dividing enterprise value by number of shares
No adjustment — they are the same

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity Value = Enterprise Value - Debt - Minority Interest - Preferred Capital + Cash + Non-operating Investments. The Trap: EV to equity is not just adding cash. You must subtract all non-equity claims and add back surplus assets. Cross-Exam Context: Tested in NISM XV Ch 10. Exam Tip: This bridge is critical in DCF valuations. FCFF model gives enterprise value; you must bridge to equity value before dividing by shares to get per-share target price.
